events.text:
**Pick: Muskegon, with Grand Haven a close second.** My ratings are below. They rest on the 2022-05-18 reports, which are 6 days old, so treat them as a guide.

| Port | Rating (0–4) | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Muskegon | 3 (good) | Boats did well in deep water (2022-05-18) |
| Grand Haven | 3 (good) | Good action over a wide depth range (2022-05-18) |
| St. Joseph | 3 for coho, 1 for Chinook | Good for coho, but kings were scarce (2022-05-18) |
| South Haven | 2 (average) | Fair fishing, fish scattered (2022-05-18) |

**How to fish it**
- **Muskegon:** The DNR said "Boats were doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water." Green and blue spoons worked well along with white flies, and a few fish came on meat rigs (Muskegon, 2022-05-18).
- **Grand Haven:** The report said "The salmon action was good 30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water." It named no lures that week (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). On 2022-05-04 salmon came on orange, black/white and glow spoons and a few on green and white flies. That report rated the fishing 1 (Grand Haven, 2022-05-04).
- **St. Joseph:** Boats fished "from 40 feet of water to well beyond 120 feet." Most fish were coho and steelhead, caught on spoons. A few Chinook and lake trout were mixed in, and the Chinook rated 1 (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18). St. Joseph has been the steadiest port. Coho fishing was rated good on 04-06, 04-13, 05-04 and 05-18.
- **South Haven:** The DNR called it "fair fishing." The fish were "spread out from 30 feet of water to deeper depths," and most boats were trolling spoons (South Haven, 2022-05-18). The two earlier May reports were rated 1 (South Haven, 2022-05-04).

**Trend:** In the north, the fish moved from shallow water to deep water in two weeks. On 2022-05-04 Grand Haven boats found Chinook in 30–60 ft and rated it 1. By 05-18 Grand Haven and Muskegon were both rated 3 in 120–240 ft (Grand Haven, 2022-05-04 and 2022-05-18; Muskegon, 2022-05-18). Buoy surface water that week was 50 F, up 6 F over the week (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-05-18).

**My read**
- I'd expect the north ports to stay good this week, since their fish had moved into deeper water by 05-18.
- The buoys show surface water at 52–53 F, down 3–4 F over the past week (current conditions for all four ports). That could mean some cooling or upwelling. I'd expect fish to shift a bit, so I'd cover a wide depth range rather than commit to one depth.
- South Haven sits between two ports that report better fishing. I'd expect it to be average at best, because the report described the fish as spread out.
- For Chinook specifically, I'd go north. St. Joseph's strength is coho.

**Caveats**
- The tool had no wind forecast and no modeled cold-layer depth, so I can't tell you whether this week's wind is safe for a small boat. Check the marine forecast before you go.
- The same-season history search returned only this year's reports, so I have no earlier-season comparison.
- Several reports say "salmon" without naming the species, so the north-port ratings may include coho and Chinook together.
